The final check — the project setting, Skip the final check and a skipped plan (MOTIR-11263)

1 · Settings › AI planning — the final check, on (the default)

A project admin (ai:configure). The Planner card gains a second SwitchRow, Run the final check, under Draft a why for each item and above the data-practice callout. On by default; on is the quiet state, with no callout. It saves with the page's shared footer on the last card, like every other row.

2 · Settings › AI planning — turned off, before Save

The admin switched it off. A yellow callout appears under the row, in the label column, saying what off means; the footer reads Unsaved changes and Save changes is enabled. The callout stays while the setting is off, saved or not.

3 · Settings › AI planning — a member without ai:configure

Read-only, exactly as the page shows its other settings: the shipped read-only banner on the first card, every switch disabled at its saved value, no footer. Shown with the final check off, so the reader also sees the callout a member gets.

4 · Planning notes — the final check is running, Skip the final check is offered

The control sits directly under the LIVE final-check head (whichever card the check is reviewing now), indented to the notes column, outside the folded list so Hide planner notes never hides it. Button secondary sm with SkipForward. Shown only to a person with ai:plan, and only while a check session is live.

4b · Planning notes — not offered at any other time (here: the fix after the check)

When no final-check session is live — a lay, a card being written, the fix, the plan proposed — there is no control. The same holds for a member who cannot steer the plan.

5 · The confirm — open

Modal alertdialog, size md, over the planning overlay. Title, description (what the final check does) and the peach consequence line (what skipping means) are the dialog's name and description. Focus lands on Keep checking, the safe answer (ring drawn statically). Tab cycles Keep checking → Skip the final check → close (×).

6 · The confirm — skipping, the request in flight

Skip the final check shows the Button's loading spinner; both buttons and × are disabled, the body is aria-busy, and Escape and a scrim click are ignored until the request answers.

7 · Skipped — the dialog closes, the notes take over

The request answered: the dialog closes and focus returns to the notes. Until the running job ends the check (within seconds), the control's place reads Skipping the final check… with a spinner (role status, read once). The check's head then turns to · done, no fix runs, and the act record says why (panel 9a).

8 · The confirm — the skip failed

The request failed (network, server). The dialog stays open with the shipped refusal line (role alert, AlertCircle in --el-danger, text --el-text). The primary reads Try again and sends the same request; Keep checking, Escape and × dismiss. Nothing changed: the check is still running.

8b · The confirm — refused: the final check had already finished

The check ended between the press and the answer, so the server refuses. The consequence line is replaced by a mint status line saying so; the only button is Close (focused). Behind the dialog the notes have already moved on to the fix or the proposed plan, and the control is gone.

9a · Proposed — the person skipped the final check

The act record's note says the check ended early and nothing was fixed; the plan is proposed as usual. The briefing's section 2 (open by default) ends with a bold line that the check was skipped, so the plan reads differently at a glance; section 5 names what the check found before the skip, unfixed.

9b · Proposed — the final check is turned off for the project

No check session ever opens, so no head, no control. The act record says the check was skipped because it is turned off for this project, and the briefing's section 2 says the plan was not checked.

9c · Proposed — the final check ran to the end (unchanged, for contrast)

Exactly as today: no line in section 2, the shipped block in section 5. This panel is drawn only so 9a and 9b can be compared with it.
